title: Selective Cross-City Transfer Learning for Traffic Prediction via Source City Region Re-Weighting

problem.claim: Effective deep traffic prediction models require large-scale traffic data, which may be unavailable in real-world scenarios.

gap.claim: Existing cross-city transfer approaches overlook source-target city divergence, allowing source models to contain noisy or harmful source knowledge.

contributions.claim: CrossTReS is a selective cross-city transfer learning framework that adaptively re-weights source regions for target fine-tuning.
The framework combines a feature network, a weighting network, and a prediction model, using domain adaptation, source-target meta-learning, and weighted source pretraining.
The learned region weights provide interpretable visualization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On real-world taxi and bike data, CrossTReS reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by up to 8% under the same settings.
The learned region weights reportedly offer interpretable visualization.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep learning is effective for complex spatio-temporal traffic prediction, but practical models need large-scale data.
Cross-city transfer can mitigate data scarcity, but existing methods overlook divergence between source and target cities.
CrossTReS selectively re-weights source regions through domain adaptation, meta-learning, and weighted source training before target fine-tuning.
The authors report gains of up to 8% over state-of-the-art baselines on real-world taxi and bike data.
The learned region weights are presented as interpretable visualizations.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact taxi and bike datasets, baseline identities, evaluation metrics, or experimental results beyond the maximum 8% improvement.
The abstract does not describe computational cost, sensitivity to source-target similarity, or failure cases.
